clue.text: So we're hurting ourselves with May still in charge (briefly) — chaos developing

definitions.note: an adverbial description: acting in a way that inflicts pain on ourselves

indicators.note: something developing is still changing shape, so these letters are being worked into a new order

parts.note: IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge, which the bracketed 'briefly' asks for

explanation.surface: A rueful Brexit-era complaint that the country keeps harming itself while Theresa May clings on amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: '(briefly)' asks for the short form of 'in charge', IC. 'developing' rearranges MAY STILL, IC and CHAOS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something that hurts you, seemingly by choice, is behaving in the manner of someone who enjoys pain.

clue.text: Various footballers cheating

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning several or sundry
footballers who fall over theatrically to win a foul are said to dive

explanation.surface: A complaint that plenty of footballers cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means several of different kinds; players who feign fouls are mocked as those who dive.

clue.text: Largely avoid turning over channel

indicators.note: turning over flips the shortened word so it reads backwards
largely means most of it, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to avoid something is to evade it

explanation.surface: Someone mostly avoids flicking to a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims EVADE to EVAD, which 'turning over' reverses. Dave is a British TV channel, and the name also nods to David Cameron, cross-referenced in 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Dave is the name of a British television station showing comedy and repeats.

clue.text: Official split stops union getting money? Blame 3 for it

definitions.note: the vote David Cameron, the 3 answer, called and is blamed for

parts.note: REF is short for referee, a match official

indicators.note: REND stops, or plugs, the gap in the union and money letters, so it sits inside them

parts.note: EU is the European Union
to rend is to tear or split

explanation.surface: A referee splits up a union squabbling over money, with a pointed finger at Cameron.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is DAVE, read as David Cameron, who called the 2016 vote on leaving the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron called the 2016 public vote on EU membership, so that ballot is what he is blamed for.

clue.text: Gross incompetence ultimately damaged 'bloody difficult woman' … ?

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and put back in a new order
ultimately points to the very end of the word incompetence

explanation.surface: A sour verdict on a famously awkward woman whose gross incompetence has done the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Clarke called Theresa May a 'bloody difficult woman'; she adopted the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monster in fairy tales is the ultimate fearsome, difficult woman.

clue.text: … revealing endlessly opportunistic politician is sham!

parts.note: to put something up is to display it, and here it is also the order to turn the next letters upwards
BOJO, Boris Johnson's nickname, cut short is BOJ; written upwards in this down light, as the preceding words instruct, those three letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: Continuing 5: exposing a self-serving politician as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as an instruction for a down light: JOB put up, i.e. turned upwards, gives BOJ, which is BOJO (Boris Johnson) without its end, as 'revealing' and 'endlessly' say.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a rigged or fraudulent arrangement, a sham dressed up as genuine.

clue.text: Law letters bit of a clue, maybe, to start of depression

parts.note: the letters of WALL STREET rearranged ('crash' as an anagram signal) spell these two words

explanation.surface: Legal correspondence, or perhaps a fragment of a puzzle clue, kicks off a bout of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a clue fragment: 'crash' is an anagram signal, so WALL STREET crashed gives LAW LETTERS, which is why the clue calls it 'bit of a clue, maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1929 New York stock market collapse set off the Great Depression of the 1930s.

clue.text: See 9
Go crazy, ha, at 5 as word spread

indicators.note: spread letters are scattered about and gathered again in a new order

parts.note: the number 5 written out as a word

explanation.surface: Someone laughs and loses it at five o'clock as news gets around.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' here is the number, not the cross-reference to OGRESS: 'as word' asks for FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a tantrum or losing one's temper is an idiom for going mad with rage.

clue.text: Two people back on tail of big cheese

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
back means this phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: a duo is a pair of people

explanation.surface: A pair of people return to back up the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big cheese' looks like a phrase meaning boss, but 'big' only gives its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch variety of the dairy food.

clue.text: Pressure on Transport Secretary at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of Secretary and also places it at the front

parts.note: a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Pressure piling up on the minister in charge of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is tension or stress put on something, the same as pressure.

clue.text: Odd service reactionary dismissed

indicators.note: reactionary suggests going backwards, so the service's letters are reversed

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A strange armed service sacks its backward-looking members.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-out is slang for weird or unconventional, as odd means strange.

clue.text: Obvious that female egghead's not far away

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
her refers to a female
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Clearly that brainy woman is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is just the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase points at a place a short distance off, there rather than here.

clue.text: English concern losing millions even

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word for concern

parts.note: a qualm is a worry or concern

explanation.surface: An English business shedding millions breaks even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' looks like a business, but it means a misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are level or balanced are the same in amount.

clue.text: Ben's holding back idiot horsemen

indicators.note: holding means one word goes inside another

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the chariot-racing hero, so Ben's surname gives HUR plus the S

indicators.note: back reads the fool's word in reverse

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Ben keeps a fool of a horseman in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben's surname is Hur, from the epic Ben-Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: Hussars were light cavalry soldiers, mounted troops on horseback.

clue.text: Negotiating teams finally suggest deal but unable to make progress

indicators.note: negotiating works things around, so these letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of suggest

explanation.surface: Negotiators at last propose a deal but the talks are stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a position with no legal move ends in deadlock, so the word means stuck without progress.

clue.text: Drug, say, affected raven and another flier

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a drug

indicators.note: affected letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: raven and jet both describe a glossy black

explanation.surface: A drug has made a raven act oddly, and another bird too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raven' looks like the bird, setting up 'another flier', but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: EasyJet is a budget airline, so it carries people through the air, another thing that flies.

clue.text: Way a strange blond misbehaved in government, as was claimed

definitions.note: describes the governing promised by a slogan; the answer is that slogan

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are out of order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd blond man behaving badly in office, contrary to promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange blond' hints at Boris Johnson. The answer was Theresa May's 2017 election slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May promised firm, steady leadership in 2017, the phrase mocked once her government faltered.

clue.text: With old PM initially get a little ratty over government relic

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns these letters upwards

parts.note: GOM, the Grand Old Man, was Gladstone's nickname
to get something is to see it

indicators.note: a little takes just the first letter of ratty

explanation.surface: An old prime minister gets a bit cross about a leftover from government.
explanation.walkthrough: Gladstone was the Grand Old Man. 'initially' says GOM leads before 'over' turns it round. Jacob Rees-Mogg is mocked as a Victorian throwback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brexiteer MP is satirised as a survival from a past age, an old relic.

clue.text: State "I want a break"

indicators.note: break smashes the letters so they reform in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares that they need a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is an island nation in East Asia, a self-governing country.

clue.text: Sketches I meticulously reviewed showing detail

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking back, so the run reads backwards
showing means the letters are on view inside the words

explanation.surface: Sketches carefully looked over reveal fine detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things one by one is to set out their particulars, a verb sense of detail.

clue.text: Disregard region's suffering

indicators.note: suffering letters are distorted into a different order

parts.note: region's stands for region is, giving the letters of the word region

explanation.surface: A region is struggling and nobody cares.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to take no notice of it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: "PM ashen," said policeman

indicators.note: said means we hear the words spoken, not written

parts.note: the prime minister May plus grey, meaning ashen

explanation.surface: A police officer remarks that the prime minister looks pale.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIGRET is said 'may-gray' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Simenon's Inspector Maigret is a fictional French detective of the Paris police.

clue.text: Change prison guard over

indicators.note: over turns the guard's word upside down in a down entry

parts.note: a warder guards prisoners

explanation.surface: The prison guard is being replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw again is to alter a boundary or plan, a change in shape.

clue.text: Member has a row about those running the show

indicators.note: about means the noise word goes round the member's letter

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
M is short for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A member of a group argues with the people in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin is short for administration, the people who manage and run an organisation.

clue.text: 'Great leader' needing help virtually at end — blooming right!

parts.note: Alexa is Amazon's virtual assistant

indicators.note: blooming opens out and changes form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-styled great leader needs help in the end; 'blooming right' is an exasperated exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' also hints at the plant alexanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king and conqueror, the original great leader.

clue.text: Leaving upsetting — wrong to sever relationship

indicators.note: upsetting tips the result upside down in a down entry
to sever is to cut through, so the cross mark goes inside the bond

parts.note: a tie is a bond or relationship
X is the mark for wrong

explanation.surface: Leaving is distressing when it cuts off a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Brexit, cutting the tie with Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is the act of leaving or departing, a noun use of the verb form.

clue.text: See 12
The French taking German drink

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: The French are drinking German beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Turned against, being taken in by fib — heinous

indicators.note: turned means the result is reversed
being taken in by means the letter for against goes inside the fib

parts.note: a lie is a fib
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Someone duped by a lie turns against it in outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned against' reads as one phrase, but 'Turned' reverses and 'against' is V.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous acts are wicked, morally monstrous ones.

clue.text: At sea — isn't following straightforward course taking back control (or why talking was difficult)

definitions.text: At sea — isn't following straightforward course

indicators.note: taking back reads the control word in reverse

parts.note: sway is power or control

explanation.surface: A Brexit gibe: 'taking back control' leaves the country adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets offer a second route: 'why talking' sounds like Y, and 'was difficult' rearranges WAS, giving Y plus AWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that yaws swings off its heading, unable to hold a steady line.
